title: Two Random Art Labels Had Zero History, Yet Schoolboys Slashed Their Own Team's Money
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Henri Tajfel (1971): Klee vs Kandinsky Paintings — How Meaningless Labels Spark Instant 'Us vs Them' Tribalism, grounded in Henri Tajfel, M. G. Billig, R. P. Bundy, Claude Flament (1971) (European Journal of Social Psychology). Empirical findings show that having survived Nazi POW camps while losing nearly his entire family in Poland, Henri Tajfel wanted to find the true zero-point of prejudice: strip away history, religion, competition, insults, and even seeing faces — then slowly ADD ingredients one by one until discrimination appeared.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: Except Tajfel NEVER GOT TO STEP TWO — because the 'empty baseline' itself exploded with instant tribalism (*Tajfel, Billig, Bundy & Flament, 1971, European Journal of Social Psychology***).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Henri Tajfel, M. G. Billig, R. P. Bundy, Claude Flament (1971). Social categorization and intergroup behaviour. European Journal of Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1002/ejsp.2420010202
- Michael Billig, Henri Tajfel (1973). Social categorization and similarity in intergroup behaviour. European Journal of Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1002/ejsp.2420030103
- Marilynn B. Brewer (1999). The Psychology of Prejudice: Ingroup Love and Outgroup Hate? Journal of Social Issues. https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-4537.00126
